concepts.name: Recency stamps
concepts.summary: Every cached value lives in an Entry that remembers the clock reading of its last use. Both reading a key and writing an existing key refresh that reading, so the entry with the smallest reading is the one used longest ago. The clock is passed in, which lets a test tick it one step per call and know exactly what each entry holds.

misconceptions.description: Thinks only set counts as a use, so reading a key leaves it looking old.

concepts.name: When eviction happens
concepts.summary: The cache drops an entry only while adding a key it does not hold yet and it is already at capacity; the check happens before the new entry goes in. Writing a key that is already cached updates the value and its recency and drops nothing.

misconceptions.description: Thinks writing an existing key on a full cache also drops an entry.
Thinks the new entry is inserted first and the cache then trims itself back to capacity.

concepts.name: Choosing the victim
concepts.summary: To drop the least recently used entry, evict has to keep the entry with the smallest last-use reading while it walks the map. The comparison in that loop decides everything: flip it and the cache throws away the entry it just used, which is the opposite of what callers rely on.

sourceRefs.needle: drops the least recently used key

misconceptions.description: Thinks the Map's insertion order already gives recency, so the loop does not matter.
Thinks dropping the most recently used entry is what an LRU cache does.
